title: Permission Denied
summary: The flag file is locked tight. But someone made a careless backup copy. Read the permission bits to find it.
story: There is a flag on this machine, kept in a vault file that only the root user can read. You are not root, so reading it head-on gives 'Permission denied'. But people are messy: backups get made, copied to odd places, and left with the wrong permissions. Somewhere on this box is a copy of that flag that anyone can read. Find it by reading the rwx bits.
objective: The vault copy is unreadable to you. Find a world-readable backup of the flag and submit it.
hints: Try to read the vault first so you see the lock: cat /home/player/vault/flag.txt . 'Permission denied' tells you the bits block you.
'ls -l' shows permissions as rwx for owner, group and others. Compare the vault file with files you CAN read.
Search the real folders for a flag file that others can read (skip the system folders like /sys and /proc): find /home /var /tmp /opt /etc -name 'flag*' -perm -o=r 2>/dev/null
